input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) The world model labelled the hydrant icon as 'Firehose', but the whiteboard and transcript show it is a physical smart fire hydrant (an IoT device collecting acoustic data), not Kinesis Data Firehose. It is transcribed as the IoT entry point (UserConsumerIOT). 2) The hydrants push correlated acoustic files daily through API Gateway, which provides authentication and security (arrow hydrant -> API Gateway). 3) API Gateway persists the files in S3 (arrow API Gateway -> S3). 4) A daily batch process on ECS processes the files from S3 as node pairs to find correlations (arrow S3 -> ECS). 5) ECS sends persistent correlations to a SageMaker ML endpoint, which assigns a leak probability (arrow ECS -> SageMaker). 6) The Analyst is drawn without an arrow, but the transcript states explicitly that the leak score from the SageMaker endpoint is fed to the human analyst team, so the Analyst is kept and connected from SageMaker. 7) Model retraining from field feedback about every six weeks is mentioned but not drawn and not attributed to a specific component, so it is recorded in notes only, with no edge. All steps form one logical flow (flow 0).

graph.name: Mueller Water Products: Water Intelligence Platform - Acoustic Leak Detection
graph.notes: Smart fire hydrants record acoustic signals on the pipe network and push the files daily through API Gateway into S3. A daily ECS batch process finds correlations and persistent correlations, which a SageMaker ML endpoint classifies with a leak probability. Human analysts review the scores. The model is retrained about every six weeks using field feedback. Benefits: less non-revenue water loss and ecological protection.

nodes.name: Smart Fire Hydrant
nodes.notes: IoT smart fire hydrants that collect acoustic data measuring noises on the pipe network. Signals are recorded daily and correlated between multiple hydrants. Part of a large-scale IoT network of meters, hydrants, pressure monitoring and water quality devices.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Receives the acoustic files pushed daily from the devices. Provides authentication and security (heavy focus on IoT security), which is why data is not pushed directly to S3.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Persists the acoustic signal files received through API Gateway.

nodes.name: ECS
nodes.notes: Daily batch process on container microservices. Processes each file as a node pair to look for correlations in the acoustic signals, including persistent correlations that occur over many days. Chosen over Lambda because the acoustic algorithms are very processor intensive.

nodes.name: SageMaker
nodes.notes: ML endpoint that classifies persistent correlations and assigns a leak probability (leak score). The model is retrained about every six weeks using feedback from the field, to reduce false positives.

nodes.name: Analyst
nodes.notes: Human analyst team that receives the leak score, reviews the persistent correlation, checks with the water utility for other nearby noise sources, and updates the leak status to 'field investigation required'.

edges.notes: Fire hydrants push correlated acoustic signal files through API Gateway daily.
After authentication and security at API Gateway, the files are pushed to and persisted in S3.
The daily ECS batch process processes each file from S3 as a node pair to look for correlations in the acoustic signals.
Persistent correlations found by ECS are sent to the SageMaker ML endpoint for classification and a leak probability.
The leak score from the SageMaker endpoint is fed to the human analyst team for further classification. Stated in the transcript; no arrow is drawn on the whiteboard.
